page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9ae.32xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC 9T95 processors clocked at 2.25 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 128 dedicated vCPUs managed via KVM virtualization, alongside 1024 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory-to-core ratio. It features a high-throughput network interface with a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware tradeoffs for this instance include the absence of dedicated graphics hardware and local disk storage. Because local storage is not provided, all persistent and scratch filesystem requirements must rely on external cloud storage volumes over the network interface. The 64 Gbps baseline network capability supports substantial I/O traffic to accommodate remote block storage volumes alongside external cluster traffic.

The dense allocation of 1024 GB RAM relative to compute capacity makes this instance type cost-effective for large-footprint, memory-bound enterprise deployments that do not require GPU acceleration. Target workloads include large in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, enterprise data analytics frameworks, real-time stream processing, and high-concurrency transactional database management systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9ae.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T95 processors running at 2.25 GHz on x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. The instance features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1024 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Network performance includes a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no onboard GPUs and contains no local instance storage, requiring remote storage volumes for all disk persistence. This architecture balances high compute capacity with an extensive memory footprint, delivering qualitative cost efficiency for organizations operating memory-dense platforms. Primary workload applications include in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise resource management backends, big data analytics, and large relational database workloads.
